critical_code_review_comments: server.py:correct_finding — the no-op short-circuit is correctly placed BEFORE recompute_derived and any DB write; returns the existing doc via Finding.from_mongo(doc). Clean.
Minor: real-correction path still sets confirmed_at on every real Correct. Not part of this fix but naming (corrected_at) would be clearer. Behavior matches spec.

seed_data_creation: Contracts and renewal_notice findings inserted directly via pymongo under freshly registered users (same pattern as test_clauseclock_stage3.py). All test data deleted in fixture teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix confirmed: correct_finding at /app/backend/server.py:434 short-circuits when `changed==[]` and returns {finding, changed_fields: [], no_change: true} without writing to DB. Regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_correct_noop_fix.py (4 tests, ~4s). Scope was intentionally narrow per E1 instructions; broader Stage 3 suite in test_clauseclock_stage3.py was not re-run.
rca of the issue: Previous implementation unconditionally set state='corrected', confirmed_at, and merged corrected_fields even when zero fields changed, inflating /accuracy corrected counts and mis-labelling untouched findings. Fix: compute `changed` diff over EDITABLE_FIELDS first; if empty, return current doc with no_change=true and skip the DB update entirely.
